title: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications with Ayo
problem: LLM-based applications consist of both LLM and non-LLM components whose combined end-to-end latency is not jointly optimized by existing frameworks, which use coarse-grained task-module orchestration that confines optimizations within individual modules.
motivation: As LLM applications grow in complexity with multi-step pipelines mixing LLM inference, retrieval, and compute stages, per-module optimization leaves significant scheduling inefficiency that compounds into high end-to-end latency.
method: Ayo breaks application pipelines into smaller pieces than existing systems do, letting it coordinate decisions across different components instead of optimizing each separately. It creates a complete map of how all parts depend on each other (called a DAG or dependency graph), then jointly optimizes when the language model runs and when the other computation happens, making the entire pipeline faster.
key_novelty: Ayo schedules the entire pipeline by optimizing language model and non-LLM parts together, rather than treating each as a separate piece to optimize independently.
contributions: Identification of the coarse-grained task-module abstraction as a bottleneck for end-to-end LLM application latency
Design of Ayo, an end-to-end optimizer with fine-grained cross-module scheduling for LLM-based applications
Demonstration of latency improvements beyond what per-module optimization can achieve

metrics.other: end-to-end latency reduction (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: existing LLM serving frameworks with per-module optimization
